title: When the Compass Burns
premise: Jonah Vasquez, a riverboat captain who keeps moving to outrun a past she refuses to name, is hired to resupply an expedition that has gone silent deep in the monsoon country. With a leaking hull, a stranger named Elias Wren who claims the expedition owes him answers, and the river rising faster than any season on record, she pushes upstream into territory where the water itself seems to remember what people want forgotten. The expedition's leader, Dr. Imara Sefu, has found something in the flooded ruins that powerful men upstream will burn villages to possess. Jonah must choose between running again and holding ground for the first time in her life; the story ends with her boat burned, the ruins drowned, and Jonah staying — captain of nothing but a village that finally knows her name.
about_author: Ansel Joubert is the pen name of a former deckhand who spent six seasons working cargo runs on tropical rivers before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on river lore, salvage culture, and the quiet violence of places where maps run out.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving Water
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She pilots her aging riverboat, the Marisol, through pre-monsoon shallows, establishing her rule: never stop longer than a job requires. A flashback hints at a town she left burning behind her. Emotional beat: restless competence masking grief.

chapters.title: A Contract Written in Rain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the port town of Callao Verde, a fixer offers triple pay to run supplies upriver to the Sefu expedition, which missed two radio check-ins. Jonah takes it despite the season. Beat: greed and curiosity overriding instinct.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias Wren forces his way aboard, claiming his sister was the expedition's cartographer. He pays in cash and lies. Jonah lets him stay, watching him too closely. Beat: wary alliance, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Leaving Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They cast off as storm clouds gather. Jonah tests Elias with river questions he answers too well for a grieving brother. First hint: he knows the expedition's route better than its manifest. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Sandbar Country
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Grounding on a shifting bar costs them a day and part of their fresh water. Working together to free the boat, they find an easy rhythm neither trusts. Beat: grudging respect.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the last relay station, the operator confirms the expedition went dark eleven days ago — and that men with corporate credentials were asking after them. Elias hides that he recognizes one name. Beat: dread compounding.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They pass a drowned mission church, and Jonah tells a half-truth about why she never stays anywhere. Elias notices the evasion. Beat: intimacy through deflection.

chapters.title: First Blood in the Water
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Pirates shadow them through a narrows; Jonah outmaneuvers them by running rapids no sane pilot would attempt. Elias realizes she'd rather die than be caught. Beat: adrenaline revealing character.

chapters.title: The Burned Village
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They reach a riverside village razed recently — the same company logo on discarded crates as at the relay station. Survivors have fled upstream. Beat: the stakes turn from missing persons to something systematic.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Inspecting the Marisol's hold, Elias finds Jonah is carrying more than supplies — old salvage, false panels, a life built for quick exits. Confrontation deferred. Beat: secrets stacked like ballast.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season Opens
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The rains arrive early and violent. The boat springs a slow leak; they bail in shifts through the night while lightning walks the ridgelines. Beat: vulnerability forced into the open.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Logbook
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hidden in the leak repair kit, Jonah finds a waterproof logbook — his sister Nadia's — planted aboard by the fixer. It shows the expedition diverted toward flooded ruins called the Sunken Terrace. Beat: betrayal and revelation entwined.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Anchor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah accuses Elias of using her; he admits he suspected the fixer was playing both sides and needed a pilot who could lie to herself. They nearly part. Beat: trust broken and barely re-forged.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Current
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They push on together, engine straining against flood current. Jonah confesses fragments of her past: a town, a fire, a man she trusted who sold the river's secrets. Beat: confession as cargo jettisoned.

chapters.title: The Company's Wake
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. They overtake a corporate gunboat anchored midriver and slip past at night, engines muffled. Elias sees mercenaries loading crates from the ruins' direction. Beat: the enemy acquires a face.

chapters.title: Nadia's Markers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Following Nadia's survey markers, they thread a flooded channel only a cartographer would chart. Jonah begins to understand Nadia's genius — and why someone wanted her silent. Beat: the absent woman becomes vivid.

chapters.title: Strangers on the Water
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. They rescue two exhausted expedition members adrift in a dugout: geologist Tomas and young intern Priya, who speak in fragments of 'the chamber' and 'Sefu's decision.' Beat: hope arriving damaged.

chapters.title: What Sefu Found
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV (interleaved). Around a rain-soaked campfire, Tomas recounts: Dr. Sefu uncovered a pre-colonial archive vault whose records map every hidden tributary and buried claim in the basin — power over land, water, and memory itself. Beat: the MacGuffin gains moral weight.

chapters.title: The Leak Wins a Round
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Marisol takes on water fast; they beach her in a mangrove cove for emergency repairs as the river climbs another meter. Beat: resourcefulness under pressure, Jonah's identity as captain tested.

chapters.title: Priya's Silence
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals she saw the mercenaries execute two porters and fled; she hasn't spoken since until now, telling Jonah because Jonah listens without pity. Beat: witness and burden shared.

chapters.title: The Sunken Terrace
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They reach the ruins rising from floodwater like a drowned crown. Smoke drifts from the far side — someone is already there. Beat: awe undercut by threat.

chapters.title: Dr. Imara Sefu
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. They find Sefu alive, barricaded in the upper terraces, guarding the vault entrance with two remaining crew. She is brilliant, ruthless, and dying of an infected wound. Beat: meeting the legend, flaws included.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sefu refuses to abandon the archive; Elias demands she surrender it if it costs lives. Stalemate. Jonah proposes a third way: move the records by boat before the mercenary company returns. Beat: negotiation as character test.

chapters.title: Reading the Flooded City
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Using Nadia's charts, Jonah plans an exit route through submerged channels that will close when the river peaks — a window of days, maybe hours. Beat: expertise finally honored.

chapters.title: The Company Returns
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Two gunboats appear downstream. Sefu's second-in-command, Ravel, is revealed as the mole who sold the expedition's position. Beat: betrayal from inside the walls.

chapters.title: Ravel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ravel's POV. Cornered, Ravel argues the archive belongs to whoever can protect it — that Sefu's secrecy doomed the porters. His corruption is seductive, almost reasonable. Beat: power's logic given a voice.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Under storm-dark, they ferry the archive crates to the Marisol in relays while Ravel signals the gunboats. The leak worsens; the river rises. Beat: desperate labor against time.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The mercenaries torch the terrace camp. In the chaos, Ravel escapes with one crate — the index to the rest. Sefu collapses from her wound. Beat: loss sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: The Running Fight
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Marisol flees downriver, outgunned. Jonah uses sandbars, side-channels, and the rising flood to break pursuit, taking a bullet graze along her ribs. Beat: the captain at the height of her craft.

chapters.title: Sefu's Confession
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Dying below decks, Sefu admits she planned to sell selective access to the archive — power corrupting even its rescuers. She gives Jonah the choice of what to do with it. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: What Belongs to the River
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah weighs Sefu's offer: wealth, leverage, a new life anywhere. She remembers every town she abandoned. Beat: the still point of the book — the choice between running and belonging.

chapters.title: The Village That Took Her In
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. They shelter at a river village that once traded with Jonah years ago; the elders remember her kindness. For the first time, Jonah is somewhere she's welcome. Beat: belonging offered, not seized.

chapters.title: Ravel's Price
chapters.summary: Ravel's POV. Ravel surfaces at the village with mercenaries, offering to spare it in exchange for the archive. The villagers look to Jonah. Beat: the cost of stopping made concrete.

chapters.title: Standing Ground
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah refuses to hand over the archive or abandon the village. She organizes the villagers, uses the flood-swollen channels, and prepares the Marisol as bait. Beat: the runner turns to fight.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Split Channel
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Jonah lures the gunboats into a closing channel where the flood current and hidden pilings wreck them; Elias and villagers capture Ravel and recover the index crate. Beat: climax — cunning, sacrifice, and community victorious.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Marisol
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Marisol burns in the fighting, taking part of the archive with her. Jonah watches her whole mobile life go up in steam and feels, strangely, unburdened. Beat: grief transmuted into release.

chapters.title: The Archive Decision
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The survivors vote: copy what remains for the villages and universities of the basin, then sink the original vault records where no company can dredge them. Sefu dies agreeing. Beat: power dissolved rather than transferred.

chapters.title: Burials and Names
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They bury Sefu above flood line; Elias finds closure over Nadia's charts and chooses to stay and teach mapping. Jonah is asked, formally, to stay. Beat: mourning becoming rootedness.

chapters.title: Learning to Be Still
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Weeks later, the flood recedes. Jonah repairs a village barge, teaches kids to read the water, and stops flinching at the word 'home.' Beat: quiet integration of all themes.

chapters.title: When the Compass Burns
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, final chapter. A new expedition arrives asking Jonah to guide them upriver — the old pull, the old itch. She looks at the village, the barge, the grave on the hill, and says no. The compass needle trembles and settles. Beat: resolution — the moving life ended not by force but by choice.
